canonical.title: Burst Balloons
canonical.sourceFilePath: 14. Dynamic Programming/8. DP on Partition/03. Burst Ballons.cpp

narrative.title: The Dominion Day Fireworks Line
narrative.scenario: A festival crew detonates a line of celebratory charges, each stamped with a potency number. Detonating a charge scores the product of its potency with its two current neighbors, and neighbors close ranks after each blast. Boundary positions pair with a fixed neutral value of 1. The pyrotechnician chooses the firing order to maximize the evening's total score.
narrative.inputFormat: An array nums of n balloon values.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the maximum coins collectable by bursting every balloon, scoring nums[i-1] * nums[i] * nums[i+1] per burst with virtual 1s at the ends.

testCases.explanation: Burst 1 first (1*5*1 = 5), then 5 (1*5*1 = 5) — total 10; bursting 5 first only reaches 6.

hintLevels: Level 1: Reason about which balloon bursts LAST in a range, not first — that decouples the two sides.
Level 2: Pad with virtual 1s; dp[i][j] = max over k of nums[i-1]*nums[k]*nums[j+1] + dp[i][k-1] + dp[k+1][j].
Level 3: The last-burst frame means k's neighbors are the range boundaries, fixed at solve time — that's why subproblems don't interfere.
